title: Best Food Photographers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a food photographer for menus, delivery apps, packaging or social media: what to include, rights, price factors and red flags.
intro: Food photography makes dishes and products look appetizing on menus, delivery apps, websites, packaging and social media. Good food photos are accurate, well lit and styled to match your brand. Shoots go wrong when the shot list is unclear, photos do not fit platform sizes, or styling makes dishes look very different from what customers receive. This guide helps you plan a shoot that sells without misleading.

faq.q: Can food photography be done remotely?
faq.a: For packaged products, yes: you ship products and the photographer shoots in their studio. For restaurant dishes, a local photographer or a remote editor working with your photos is more practical.
Arranging food, props and backgrounds so dishes look their best on camera. Some photographers style, others work with a stylist.

faq.q: Which sizes do delivery apps need?
faq.a: Each platform has its own requirements. Share them so photos are shot and cropped correctly.

faq.q: Can photos be edited to look better?
faq.a: Light and color correction is normal. Making portions look larger or changing ingredients misleads customers.
Agree on usage rights: menus, website, delivery apps, ads and packaging, and for how long.
